rationale: Plural noun in the phrase ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ϣⲁϩϣϥ̄ 'in five ⲛ̄ϣⲁϩϣϥ̄' describing the Magousaean seven-headed dragon coiled in its cave. Etymology unclear: possibly a Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱϣϥ̄ 'destroy, scatter' giving 'scatterings'; or related by metathesis to ⲥⲁϣϥ̄ 'seven.' Could also designate the dragon's coils/limbs. Confidence low; awaits parallel attestation.

Lycopolitan reflex of Greek δράκων with metathetic loss of δ-onset (compare standard Coptic ⲇⲣⲁⲕⲱⲛ in glossary). Recurs throughout this kephalaion as the central figure of the Magousaean myth that the Apostle reinterprets pneumatically as the seven sense-organs.

proposed_english: the place of seeing / the eye
rationale: Compound: ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ̄ (Lyc. for ⲱⲣϩ̄ 'see, watch'). Standard Coptic formation parallel to glossary entries ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'place of hearing' and ⲡⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲗⲙⲉ 'place of smelling.' The eye as the cosmic 'place-of-seeing' — direct organ-as-locus designation.

ⲥⲁϣϩⲃⲉ likely an abstract noun on ⲥⲁϣϥ̄/ⲥⲁϣϥⲉ 'seven' with -ϩⲃⲉ extension; possibly related to ⲥⲁϣϩⲉ in L27, 31. Designates the seven-fold quality of the dragon's head, decoded as the seven sense-organs.

ⲡⲕⲉ- ('the also/other') + ⲗⲉⲥ (Lyc. for ⲗⲁⲥ 'tongue'). The seventh sense-organ in the head, completing the count after the three sense-pairs (eyes/ears/nostrils). ⲕⲉ- carries connective force 'and likewise.'

Plural noun for 'tastes,' likely Lyc. plural of ϯⲡⲉ 'taste' (see glossary ⲧϯⲡⲉ 'the taste'). Object of the tongue's discrimination: 'taking in it the tastes which are varied that exist in every likeness.'
